label: Gateway Simulator
info: Simulates Edge Gateway A publishing Sparkplug B NBIRTH, DBIRTH, DDATA, and DDEATH lifecycle telemetry messages to Mosquitto MQTT broker. Read the on-canvas comment nodes for a walkthrough of how to onboard your own device, register a gateway, and approve a quarantined device -- see simulators/README.md for the full write-up.

name: Guide on setting up a Gateway and Device
NBIRTH
info: The edge node's own birth certificate. Real Sparkplug B requires this once before any DBIRTH. This app's ingestion (process_node_message) treats NBIRTH/NDATA identically for gateway status, so it isn't strictly required here -- but real brokers/hosts expect the order below.

name: 1. Trigger NBIRTH Node Birth Certificate (once at startup)
Build NBIRTH Certificate (Virtual_Gateway_NodeRED)
ADD YOUR OWN DEVICE:
info: 1) Create the device in the app's Devices tab and copy the Sparkplug ID it is issued (24 characters, 'dev' + 21 hex). 2) Put that id in the topic's last path segment and in the Asset_ID metric -- the topic is what identifies the device; Asset_ID is a cross-check and a mismatch quarantines it. 3) Set Asset_Name to whatever you want the device called; it is a label only and the app never overwrites its own name from it. 4) Replace the metric list with your device's real telemetry. 5) Deploy. An id the app does not know lands in the quarantine queue; one that is the wrong length or shape lands there too, with a message saying exactly how it is malformed.

name: COMPLETE THE LOOP -- Approve the device
info: On first DBIRTH, an unrecognized device is auto-inserted into the devices table as quarantined (is_quarantined = true) and its DDATA is silently dropped until approved. Open the app -> Devices tab -> 'Zero-Touch Onboarding Quarantine Queue' and Approve (or Reject) it as an Administrator or Shopfloor_Manager.

REGISTER THE GATEWAY FIRST:
info: unlike devices, gateways are never auto-created. Create a gateway in the app's Gateways tab (Administrator or Shopfloor_Manager), copy the Sparkplug ID it is issued, and use that as the edge node segment of the topic. This flow ships with 'gwy100000000000400080000', which is the id of the pre-seeded Virtual_Gateway_NodeRED row -- its UUID is pinned in migration 0009 precisely so this flow can hardcode it. An unrecognised edge node is logged and dropped.

name: Build NDATA Gateway Heartbeat
Quarantine Webhook Receiver
info:
Receives POST /hooks/quarantine from Supabase.

Fired by the trg_device_quarantine_webhook trigger on public.devices
(supabase/migrations/20260101000027_quarantine_webhook.sql) via pg_net, and only when a
device ENTERS quarantine -- not on every device write, and not on gateway heartbeats.

The endpoint URL is registered in public.webhook_endpoints; changing it there is enough,
no flow edit required. If NODERED_ADMIN_TOKEN is set the request carries a bearer token
read from Supabase Vault; on the default stack Node-RED has no adminAuth and the request
arrives unauthenticated.

pg_net is fire-and-forget: no retries, no ordering, no dead-letter queue. Treat this as
an advisory notification, not a delivery guarantee -- see the migration header.

name: Log Quarantine Event
NCMD REBIRTH (Sparkplug Node Control/Rebirth)
info:
The ingestion daemon holds each edge node's metric ALIAS TABLE in memory, so it is empty after every restart -- and a stable device may not birth again for hours. When it meets a DDATA metric carrying an alias it cannot resolve, it publishes `Node Control/Rebirth` to spBv1.0/<group>/NCMD/<edge_node>, rate limited to one request per node per REBIRTH_REQUEST_INTERVAL_SECONDS.

This listener is what makes that recovery work end to end. Without it the daemon asks and nothing answers, and alias-optimised telemetry stays undecodable until the next scheduled DBIRTH.

label: Multi-Standard Shopfloor
info:
# Multi-Standard Shopfloor Simulator

Five devices across four cell gateways, each publishing a different companion standard over
Sparkplug B.

| Cell | Device | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CNC Machining | CNC_Mill_01, CNC_Mill_02 | MTConnect 2.x |
| CNC Machining | CNC_Mill_01 (KPIs) | ISO 22400 |
| Robotic Assembly | Robot_Arm_01 | OPC 40010 Robotics + 40001-4 Energy |
| AGV Marshalling | AGV_01 | OPC 40010 (flattened state) |
| Site-Wide | BMS_Zone_01 | ASHRAE 223P |

**One MQTT connection per gateway.** `mosquitto.acl` pins the topic's edge-node segment to the
connecting username, so devices cannot share a broker node across cells.

**Every metric name is registered in `metric_catalog`** (migrations 0018, 0019) with its
standard and published semantic id. Publishing an unregistered name creates an orphaned series.

Generated by `scripts/generate-simulator-flow.mjs` -- edit that, not this tab.

name: FAULT INJECTION -- click the button on the left of a node to fire it
info:
These set a GLOBAL flag that every device subflow reads on its next scan. They are global
rather than wired because a fault is a property of the scenario, not of one node -- and the
thermal excursion has to be visible to both CNC_Mill_01 and the OEE aggregator, which are
different subflow instances and cannot see one another's context.

Effects, all within one 5-second scan:

- Thermal: `Systems/TEMPERATURE` on CNC_Mill_01 -> ~95 degC. OEE quality falls because scrap
  rises, so `OEE/OEE` follows on the next 60-second KPI publish.
- E-stop: `MotionDevice/EmergencyStop` true, `Machine/OperationalMode` STOPPED,
  `Controller/EXECUTION` INTERRUPTED, `Controller/EMERGENCY_STOP` TRIGGERED. Availability
  falls because the machine stops accumulating productive time.
- Reset clears both.
